trial_court: V Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru - M.C.No.2533/2016
case_name: Mr Shrikant Saboo vs Mrs Meghna Saboo on 16 February, 2023
facts_of_case: Petitioner-husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia)&(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act. Respondent-wife filed a petition for maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking interim maintenance to establish that they are in need of such relief.
legal_principles.held: It is stated that the children are studying in school and respondent is paying the school fees by raising loan from her relatives. Hence, the petitioner is liable to pay the interim maintenance as sought by the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A party's luxurious lifestyle and ability to pay can be considered while determining the amount of interim maintenance.
legal_principles.held: He is leading a luxurious life, such as, every year he used to go to foreign countries on trips...

legal_principles.principle: A party's income and expenses should be considered while determining the amount of interim maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court has not taken into consideration the annual income of the petitioner and has awarded lesser maintenance amount.

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to pay towards the maintenance of their children can be considered while determining the amount of interim maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The petitioner has not paid a single pie towards the maintenance of the children.

outcome.final_order: The court modified the impugned order and enhanced the interim maintenance.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
